solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrangement for art-house distribution

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: Talk of how an independent cinema film gets released to arthouse screens.
explanation.definitionFit: A share-out is the act of dividing something among people, a noun synonym for distribution.

clue.text: Ensnare a smoker

definitions.note: a hooka (hookah) is a water pipe, something one smokes from

parts.note: to hook a fish or a person is to ensnare it

explanation.surface: Catch someone who smokes, perhaps in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: The hookah, also spelt hooka, is an oriental water pipe, so a smoking device stands in as a 'smoker'.

clue.text: Substitute set to appear after second match almost finished

indicators.note: says the word for set comes after the shortened match
almost means the final letter of the word is not used

parts.note: a replay is a second playing of a drawn match
to cement something is to set it firm

explanation.surface: A football substitute is told to come on after a drawn replay is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second match' is a replay, the rerun of a drawn cup tie; 'set' is the verb, as concrete or cement sets hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement is a person or thing taking another's place, a direct synonym of substitute.

clue.text: Gloomy director's position in theatre?

definitions.meaning: a stage director is in charge of, so placed over, the cast

explanation.surface: A dark mood around where a theatre director stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast weather is grey and dim; read as two words it puts the director above the actors.

clue.text: Punishes sailors with contaminated fresh tea

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
and means together with

indicators.note: contaminated letters are spoiled and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A captain disciplines the crew by serving them spoiled tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarring and feathering was a mob's humiliating punishment, so the phrase is used for punishing someone severely.

clue.text: Instructions on what's regularly used by chippies

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as on does

indicators.note: only every other letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Guidance on what carpenters, or fish-and-chip shops, routinely use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippies' is British slang for carpenters and for chip shops. 'regularly used by' takes C, I, P, E from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of directions for preparing a dish, hence instructions.

clue.text: Drivers one's seen on motorway showing unacceptable prejudice

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation for drivers
one is I, and 's stands for is, so IS
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Motorists on a motorway behave with open bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the British Royal Automobile Club, a breakdown service for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Racism is discrimination based on race, a prejudice that is widely condemned as unacceptable.

clue.text: What group of scouts mostly raised perhaps?

definitions.text: What group of scouts mostly raised perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read upward, so backwards
mostly drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: a pack is a group of Cub Scouts

explanation.surface: A riddle: what might a troop of scouts lift?
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PACK to PAC; 'raised' turns it upward. The whole clue also defines: a cap is what one raises, and scouts wear caps.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a hat that is raised or doffed in greeting, so it is something raised.

clue.text: Successfully tested class, securing good grade in French language

parts.note: something proven has been tested and shown sound

indicators.note: securing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
an A is a top grade in an exam

explanation.surface: A pupil who passed the class earns a top grade in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal is the Occitan dialect spoken in Provence, a language of southern France.

clue.text: Chap's rear squeezed into short item of underwear: laugh uncontrollably

indicators.note: squeezed into means placed inside the other piece
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a corset is a tight foundation garment

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A man's backside crammed into a corset is enough to make anyone crack up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CORSET to CORSE; 'rear' gives the last letter of Chap. In theatre slang an actor who corpses breaks into helpless laughter on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang: to corpse is to break character with uncontrollable laughter.

clue.text: Old person, heading off towards port reportedly, finding shellfish supplier?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an old crock is a decrepit elderly person

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: Poole is a harbour town in Dorset, England

explanation.surface: An old-timer heads toward the harbour in search of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' cuts CROCK to ROCK. Poole is a south-coast English port; said aloud it matches POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool among seashore rocks holds crabs, winkles and limpets, so the question mark admits it is a playful source of shellfish.

clue.text: A rodent from tail to head is so long

indicators.note: reading from tail to head runs the letters backwards

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat measured nose to tail is this long.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ra is an informal British farewell, a synonym of the parting phrase so long.

clue.text: Secret group I dismissed, right away

parts.note: a class is a group or category

indicators.note: away means that letter is taken out

parts.note: an employee fired is dismissed

explanation.surface: A clandestine cell I was sacked from, and correctly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes R out of FIRED, leaving FIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are officially restricted, kept secret from the public.

clue.text: Long suffering soldiers mostly exhausted, invading European country

indicators.note: invading means going inside the other piece

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
OR (other ranks) means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: dead beat means exhausted, so beat

explanation.surface: Worn-out troops endure as they march into a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', soldiers below officers; 'exhausted' is 'dead beat', trimmed by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance is patient self-restraint, enduring provocation, which long suffering also describes.

clue.text: Defamed a journalist backing press changes

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so this piece goes at the end
changes signals that the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter supports changes to the press after being slandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but places the editor behind the reworked press.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast slurs on someone's reputation, so aspersed means slandered.

clue.text: Prudish girl attracted to Mennonite sect, without question

indicators.note: attracted to means drawn next to the following piece
without in its old sense means outside, so the girl's name goes round

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
the Amish are a strict Mennonite group

explanation.surface: A strait-laced young woman is drawn to the Amish, no questions asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' surrounds Q with SUE, giving SQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish can mean easily shocked or offended by impropriety, close to prudish.

clue.text: Hit, throwing stone in brawl

indicators.note: throwing means casting off, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: struck means hit
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone is struck when stones fly in a street fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' removes ST (stone, a British weight of 14 pounds) from STRUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruck is a rough scrum or melee, so a brawl.

clue.text: Political reformer enlisted by US socialists in area of N America

indicators.note: enlisted by means taken inside the other group

parts.note: Labor is the American spelling of Labour, the left-wing party
a rad, short for radical, is a political reformer

explanation.surface: A reforming politician joins American leftists somewhere in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland region of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

clue.text: Project with European material

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

explanation.surface: A scheme with European fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute is a coarse plant fibre woven into sacking, a material.

clue.text: Former duke enters Cambridgeshire city in joyful fashion

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: A one-time duke strolls into Ely in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elatedly means with great happiness, an adverb for a joyful manner.

clue.text: Songbird to flutter, chasing rail

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes second

parts.note: a bar is a rail, as on a fence
a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: A little bird flits after a railing.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbet is a tropical bird with a stout bill, named here as a songbird.

clue.text: Expert's way accepted by Pamela and Daisy

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: Pam is short for Pamela
ST, short for street, is a way
the aster is a daisy-like flower of the daisy family

explanation.surface: An expert's method is welcomed by two women, Pamela and Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is someone highly skilled in an activity, an expert.

clue.text: Composer's brief to supply modern music

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: A composer's concise brief to produce contemporary music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' shortens RAVEL to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rave is electronic dance music from the late 1980s onward, a modern style.

clue.text: Very mature red ultimately missing in cellar

indicators.note: missing means that letter is left out

parts.note: an adult is mature

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A very aged red wine has gone from the wine cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives D, the last letter of red; 'missing' removes it from ADULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is an underground storage room, such as a wine cellar.

clue.text: Obedient tot gets back into good book

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: the Good Book is the Bible

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A child is returned to a decent book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb to tot up; 'back' turns ADD into DDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Biddable means willing to do as one is bid, so obedient.

clue.text: Monk last to leave part of cathedral

indicators.note: the final letter of the word departs

parts.note: a dome is the rounded roof of a cathedral

explanation.surface: A monk is the last to depart from a section of the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Dom is a title given to Benedictine and some other monks.

clue.text: Down under, real scandal about injecting fluid

indicators.note: injecting means put inside the other piece
about means the word is turned round

parts.note: mud, as in mudslinging, is scandal
ink is a fluid

explanation.surface: An Australian exposé about a genuine scandal involving drugs injected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' marks the definition as Australian slang; mud stands for scandal as in mudslinging.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinkum is Australian slang for genuine or honest, as in fair dinkum.

clue.text: Motif at entrance to this art museum

parts.note: a motif is a recurring theme

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A design spotted at the door of this gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met is the usual name for the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

clue.text: Thus row hasn't finished about accommodation cost in Italian resort

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece
the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: row is taken as written
rent is what one pays for accommodation

explanation.surface: An argument over room charges at a seaside town in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' cuts ROW to RO, which goes 'about' RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a holiday town on the Bay of Naples in Italy.
